title: cDNA AND GENE FOR HUMAN ANGIOGENIN (ANGIOGENESIS FACTOR) AND METHODS OF EXPRESSION
abstract: DNA sequences encoding a protein having angiogenic activity. Expression vectors containing these sequences are introduced into host cells and direct the production of the angiogenic protein. Proteins produced according to the invention are useful in the diagnosis of malignancies, for promoting wound healing, and for other diagnostic and therapeutic purposes.

description: cDNA AND GENE FOR HUMAN ANGIOGENIN (ANGIOGENESIS FACTOR) AND METHODS OF EXPRESSION Field of the Invention This invention relates to protein production through recombinant DNA techniques. More particularly, it relates to DNA sequences encoding proteins having aπgiogenic activity and to methods of expressing those sequences. Background Art 5 Aπgiogenesis, the process of developing a hemovascular network, is essen¬ tial for the growth of solid tumors and is a component of normal wound healing and growth processes. It has also been implicated in the pathophysiology of atherogenesis, arthritis, and diabetic retinopathy. It is characterized by the directed growth of new capillaries toward a specific stimulus. This 10 growth, mediated by the migration of endothelial cells, may proceed independently of endothelial cell mitosis. The molecular messengers responsible for the process of angiogenesis have long been sought. Greenblatt and Shubik (J. Natl. Cancer Inst. 41; 111-124, ** -- * ' 1968) concluded that tumor-induced ne vascularization is mediated by a diffus¬ ible substance. Subsequently, a variety of soluble mediators have been impli¬ cated in the induction of neovascularization. These include prostaglandins (Auerbach, in Lymphokines, Pick and Landy, eds., 69-88, Academic Press, New York, 1981), human urokinase (Berman et al., Invest Opthalm. Vis. Sci. 22; 20 191-199, 1982), copper (Raju et al., J. Natl. Cancer Inst. 69; 1183-1188, 1982), and various "angiogenesis factors". Angiogenesis factors have been derived from tumor cells, wound fluid - • (Baπda et al., Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci USA 79; 7773-7777, 1982; Banda et al., 25 United States Patent 4,503,038), and retinal cells (D'Amore, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 78; 3068-3072, 1981). Tumor-derived angiogenesis factors have in general been poorly characterized. Folkman et al. (J. Exp. Med. 133; 275-288, - 2 - 197.1.)' isolated a tumor angiogenesis factor from the Walker 256 rat ascit tumor. The factor was mitogenic for capillary endothelial cells and w inactivated by RNase. Tuan et al. (Biochemistry 12; 3159-3165, 1973) fou mitogenic and angiogenic activity in the nonhistone proteins of the Walker 2 5 tumor. The active fraction was a mixture of proteins and carbohydrate. variety of animal and human tumors have been shown to produce angiogenes factor(s) (Phillips and Kumar, Int. J. Cancer 23; 82-88, 1979) but the chem cal! nature of the factor(s) was not determined. A low molecular weight no protein component from Walker 256 tumors has also been shown to be angiogen 10. and ; mitogenic (Weiss et al., Br. J. Cancer 40; 493-496, 1979). An angi genesis factor with a molecular weight of 400-800 daltons was purified homogeneity by Fenselau et al. (J. Biol. Chem. 256; 9605-9611, 1981), but was,- nσt further characterized. Human lung tumor cells have been shown secrete an angiogenesis factor comprising a high molecular weight carrier a 15 a low molecular weight, possibly non-protein, active component (Kumar et al Int. J. Cancer 32; 461-464, 1983). Vallee et al. (Experientia. 41; 1-1 1985). found angiogenic activity associated with three fractions from Walk 256 tumors. Tolbert et al. (United States Patent 4,229,531) disclose t production of angiogenesis factor from the human adenocarcinoma cell line H 20 - 29*,, but the material was only partially purified and was not chemically cha acterized. Isolation of genes responsible for the production of angiogenes factors has not heretofore been reported at least in part due to the lack purity and characterization of the factors. • " - Isolation of angiogenesis factors has employed high performance liqu chromatography (Banda et al., ibid); solvent extraction (Folkman. et al ibid); chromatography on silica gel (Fenselau et al., ibid), DEAE cellulo (Weiss et al., ibid), or Sephadex (Tuan et al., ibid); and affinity chromat graphy (Weiss et al., ibid). - 3 - Recently, Vallee et al . (United States Patent Application Serial No . 724 , 088 , filed April 17 , 1985 , and USSN __, filed concurrently with this application, both of which are hereby incorporated by reference) have purufied an angiogenic protein from a human adenocarcinoma cell line . The purified protein, known as angiogenin, was chemically characterized and its- a ino acid sequence determined. Because angiogenesis factors play an important role in wound healing (Rettura et al. , FASEB Abstract #4309, 61st Annual Meeting, Chicago, 1977) and may find applicability in the development of screening tests for malignancies (Klagsbrun e a i. _ Cancer Res. 36; 110-114, 1976; and Brem et al. , Science 195;. 880-881, 1977) , it would clearly be advantageous to produce angiogenic proteins In sufficient quantities to permit their application in therapy and diagnosis. The techniques of genetic engineering are Ideally suited to increase production levels of these proteins. The cloning of genes enco d ing angiogenic proteins Is a necessary first step in such large-scale production. Furthermore, It may in some instances be desirable to obtain these proteins from non-tumor cells, such as in the case of human therapeutics, where contamination with certain tumor products would be unacceptable. This Invention therefore provides for the production of angiogenic proteins in non- tumor cells using recombinant DNA techniques. Disclosure of the Invention Briefly stated, the present invention discloses a DNA sequence encoding a protein having angiogenic activity. A DNA sequence encoding angiogenin, or a protein having substantially the same biological activity as angiogenin, is also disclosed . The DNA sequences may be obtained from cDNA or genomic DNA, or may be prepared by DNA synthesis techniques . The invention further discloses vectors comprising a DNA sequence encod¬ ing a protein having angiogenic activity. Vectors comprising a DNA sequence encoding a protein having substantially the same biological activity as _ 4 _ angiogenin are also disclosed. The vectors further comprise a promo sequence upstream of and operably linked to the DNA sequence. In general, vectors will also contain a selectable marker, and, depending on the host c used, may contain such elements as regulatory sequences, polyadenylat signals, enhancers, and RNA splice sites. An additional aspect of the present invention discloses cells transfec or: transformed to produce a protein having angiogenic activity. Cells tra fected or transformed to produce a protein having substantially the s Q , biological activity as angiogenin are also disclosed. The cells transfected or transformed to contain an expression vector comprising a sequence encoding a protein having angiogenic activity. A further aspect of the present invention discloses' a method for prod 5 ing a protein having angiogenic activity. The method comprises (a) Introd ing into a host cell a vector comprising a DNA sequence encoding a prot having angiogenic activity; (b) growing the host cell In an appropri medium; and (c) Isolating the protein product encoded by the DNA sequence produced by the host cell. A method for producing a protein having substan 0 ally the same biological activity as angiogenin is also disclosed. ' proteins produced by these methods are also disclosed. Biological activity is a function or set of functions performed molecule in a biological context (i.e. , in an organism or an in v facsimile) . For angiogenin, biological activity is characterized by angiogenic activity. Angiogenic activity is the chemical stimulation of hemovascular development in tissue . It is generally associate with diffusible substances produced by a variety of cell types Angiogenic activity may be characterized by a positive respons in the chick embryo chorioallantoic membrane assay (Knighton e al. , Br. Angiogenic proteins are produced by a variety of cell types, incl tumor cells and retinal cells. Until recently, these proteins have not obtained in sufficient purity to permit their chemical and physical chara ization. Through the application of a novel multi-step purification pr cedure, an exemplary angiogenic protein, hereinafter angiogenin, has be purified from culture media of a human tumor cell line. Determination of t protein sequence has allowed the isolation of corresponding DNA sequences a the expression of these sequences through recombinant DNA techniques . The Isolation of angiogenic proteins is based on the fractionation conditioned cell media by ion exchange chromatography, followed by hi performance liquid chromatography.
